verdict.rationale: Cognee's recall() docs imply that developers can specify a search type and choose among retrieval strategies instead of relying on one fixed similarity search, since it only auto-selects a strategy when none is given. A founder's community comment adds that nodesets work like tags and that graph filtering is available, but no first-party docs describe metadata-filter parameters. missing for 10: an explicit documented list of search types (keyword/hybrid modes), documented metadata/tag filter parameters, any reranking capability, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can steer retrieval with metadata filters, keyword/hybrid search modes, or reranking instead of accepting a single fixed similarity search

citations.quote: when you do not specify a search type, `recall()` classifies the query and picks the best retrieval strategy automatically
It searches memory using the best available source for the request.
cognee has notion of nodesets which work similar to tags... we have graphs per user now available. So, user permissions + graph filtering.
